sources.title: 100,000,000,000,000 Dollars, Zimbabwe, 2008
sources.locator: National Museum of American History, object 2015.0071.1. Obverse Text, Description and Related Dates.
sources.supports: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe banknote is denominated at 100 trillion Zimbabwe dollars. The obverse bears Harare and 2008. The catalogue dates manufacture to 2008.

cards.title: The note’s denomination and printed date
cards.text: The Smithsonian catalogues Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe note 2015.0071.1. Its face says 100,000,000,000,000 dollars, Harare and 2008.
cards.limits: The face dates the inscription. An issue notice can give the first circulation date. A price record for a named place and date can show what this amount could buy there.

exhibits.name: 100 trillion Zimbabwe dollars
exhibits.dateKind: Date printed on the banknote. The catalogue also dates manufacture to 2008.
exhibits.summary: Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe. National Museum of American History, National Numismatic Collection, 2015.0071.1. The printed sum is in Zimbabwe dollars. Compare a dated price record to find how far that sum reached at a particular sale.
exhibits.altText: Original diagram of a green catalogue mount for a paper note. The museum record on this case identifies the denomination and printed date.

items.name: Oduya’s signed goods voucher
items.description: The voucher names exact quantities. Oduya put those goods aside in Emberford and keeps them there until collection.

items.name: Corvan’s signed co-op credit
items.description: Eight co-op credits for goods at the open counter in Emberford. The dated review clause can bring another three credits at the next service bell.

missions.title: Three Goods, Two Bells
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What can a signed promise fix when market prices move?
missions.stake: The Emberford co-op needs oil, wicks and flour for its evening workbench. A reserve shelf holds stock aside. The open counter lets the crew adjust what it takes home.

objectives.title: Seal a basket and quote it at both dated bells.
Sign a goods voucher or a reviewable credit.
Use the signed ticket at its Emberford counter.

hints.text: Dagny’s basket bench is beside the banknote case in Lantern Square.
The co-op puts one of each good in the basket. Pick one more good and seal the basket.
Each rail has prices from a different day. Keep the basket sealed while you bring both quotes to the bench.
Use the Day 1 and Day 2 quote buttons with the same sealed basket. The co-op credit amount stays at eight.
The co-op signs for goods at one counter and a credit amount at another.
Oduya can put the exact goods aside. Corvan can offer a range of goods at the current price.
Look at what moved between bells. A voucher fixes the quantities and ties up stock. Credit lets you change the mix or wait for the review.
At Dagny’s bench choose Sign the goods voucher or Sign reviewable credit. The ticket travels in your bag.
Take the co-op ticket to Emberford by the usual Nexus crossing.
Look for Oduya’s shelf near the north bench or Corvan’s open counter east of the fountain.
The voucher collects the sealed basket. On the credit route pack a mix you can afford, or use the dated review for the next service bell.
Collect the reserved basket from Oduya or select goods and settle at Corvan’s counter. The checked stock receipt stays there.

journal.text: The same co-op basket used two dated prices. Its first and second value differed. At the receiving counter the voucher preserved quantities, while the credit preserved a sum until its dated review.

chronicle.title: The reserved basket
chronicle.text: Oduya kept the named goods aside. The crew collected that basket and released its shelf.

chronicle.title: The checked credit
chronicle.text: Corvan kept the goods and the current bell on the receipt. Any leftover credit stayed with the co-op.
